summary: The core contact-reduction argument through (8) is mathematically sound, but the candidate does not verify all predecessor hypotheses and its final two-routing calibration contains claims not established by the supplied fact.
gaps: Before invoking accepted fact 65512ded3a06d971, the proof never checks its required hypothesis 0<t<a_1+m. This does follow from the residual strip (for example s>1-r gives M<a_1+m, hence t=2(M+a_1+m)/9<a_1+m), but the applicability check is absent. The analogous range hypothesis for applying d2d117bcc58a1ba0 in the 74e60bee4b401289 calibration is also not checked in the candidate.

The last calibration asserts that the two support-extreme reflected routes in accepted fact 74e60bee4b401289 are not selected from the contact sets U_q(b) after fixing the unique optimizer, and then says that the example rules out replacement by a fixed allocation. The supplied accepted fact computes neither a_*(q), b=t-a_*(q), nor the argmax sets U_q(b), and the candidate supplies no calculation or argument connecting the reflected route caps to those argmax sets. The fact only proves failure of its particular two-route witness while the true depth region is nonempty, so these stronger contact-set and fixed-allocation assertions are unsupported.
repair_hints: Verify the allocation-range hypothesis explicitly from the residual inequalities before using 65512ded3a06d971, and verify the numerical profile-range hypothesis before using d2d117bcc58a1ba0 in the second calibration.

For the two-routing calibration, compute or otherwise characterize the actual optimizer a_*(q), the residual demand b, and U_q(b) in the relevant directions, then prove the claimed nonmembership. Separately justify any claim about all fixed allocations; the failure of the two displayed reflected routes alone does not establish it.
